title: Primary Official Registries, Statistical Agencies & Open Telemetry
description: Primary-source documentary repositories, court dockets, audited regulatory disclosures, statistical bureaus, and physical telemetry sensors used to anchor journalistic reporting in hard ground truth.

sources.name: UN OCHA ReliefWeb
sources.ownership_and_funding: Humanitarian information service operated by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
sources.editorial_standards: Aggregates official UN agency situation reports (UNHCR, WFP, UNICEF), IPC famine classifications, and vetted humanitarian NGO field assessments with exact publication timestamps.
strengths: Primary humanitarian situation reports, displacement counts, food-insecurity phases (IPC), and disaster impact maps
Open REST API for structured retrieval by date, country, and disaster type
known_limitations_and_biases: UN agencies frequently rely on host-government ministries for baseline access or raw figures—always inspect footnote provenance inside UN sitreps
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Check whether the sitrep's underlying figure comes from independent UN field verification or unverified host-ministry reporting; pair with satellite/OSINT collectives.

sources.name: ICJ & ICC Official Court Dockets
sources.ownership_and_funding: Principal judicial organ of the United Nations (ICJ) and treaty-based International Criminal Court (ICC, https://www.icc-cpi.int).
sources.editorial_standards: Verbatim primary judicial orders, provisional measures, dissenting judicial opinions, state memorials, and arrest-warrant applications.
strengths: Eliminates widespread media misreporting of international court rulings (e.g., confusing 'plausibility' at a provisional-measures stage with a final merits judgment)
known_limitations_and_biases: Party submissions/memorials reflect adversarial legal advocacy by claimant/respondent states—only Orders and Judgments of the Court represent judicial findings
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Read the exact operative paragraphs ('dispositif') of the Court's Order alongside specialist doctrinal analysis (e.g., Lawfare, EJIL:Talk!).

sources.name: U.S. SEC EDGAR & Audited Securities Filings
sources.ownership_and_funding: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission federal public disclosure system.
sources.editorial_standards: Statutory securities-fraud liability (Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F for foreign private issuers, S-1) audited by PCAOB-registered accounting firms.
strengths: Ground-truth revenue exposure, supply-chain concentration risks, material cybersecurity breach disclosures (8-K Item 1.05), litigation contingencies, and executive compensation
Free JSON REST API without authentication keys (requires descriptive User-Agent header)
known_limitations_and_biases: Covers publicly listed issuers; Risk Factor sections use broad defensive legal boilerplate alongside genuine disclosures
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Compare footnote accounting policies and Non-GAAP reconciliations against FT/WSJ financial reporting.

sources.name: IMF Data, World Bank Open Data & Federal Reserve FRED
sources.ownership_and_funding: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), International Monetary Fund (https://data.imf.org), and World Bank Group (https://data.worldbank.org).
sources.editorial_standards: Standardized SNA/BPM6 macroeconomic statistical series with explicit seasonal-adjustment, revision-history (ALFRED), and national-statistical-office metadata.
strengths: Canonical time series for CPI/PCE inflation, sovereign debt-to-GDP, balance of payments, yield curves, labor force participation, and poverty baselines
known_limitations_and_biases: International series depend on member-state statistical submissions, which vary in quality or face political manipulation in authoritarian/capacity-constrained states; initial GDP/payroll prints undergo scheduled revisions
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Always check real vs. nominal units, seasonal adjustment, per-capita scaling, and data-revision vintage before citing macro figures.

sources.name: WHO Disease Outbreak News, CDC MMWR & ECDC
sources.ownership_and_funding: World Health Organization, U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr), and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.
sources.editorial_standards: International Health Regulations (IHR) case definitions, laboratory-confirmed vs. suspected case stratification, and genomic clade surveillance.
strengths: Primary case counts, case-fatality denominators, genomic sequencing summaries, and public-health emergency notifications
known_limitations_and_biases: Early outbreak reports suffer from severe testing/ascertainment lag and member-state reporting delays, which artificially inflate naive early Case Fatality Ratios (CFR) relative to true Infection Fatality Ratios (IFR)
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Pair official surveillance bulletins with STAT News / Nature News reporting and peer-reviewed epidemiological seroprevalence models.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) & NIST NVD
sources.ownership_and_funding: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and National Institute of Standards and Technology (https://nvd.nist.gov).
sources.editorial_standards: Standardized CVE identifiers, CVSS severity scoring, MITRE ATT&CK technique mappings, and verified active in-the-wild exploitation flags.
strengths: Ground-truth technical confirmation of whether a software vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild versus merely theoretical
Joint international cybersecurity advisories (Five Eyes, ENISA, JPCERT)
known_limitations_and_biases: NVD enrichment backlogs can delay CVSS vector updates on newly minted CVEs; nation-state attribution in joint advisories summarizes classified telemetry not fully visible in public packets
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Cross-reference CVE advisories with independent security researcher write-ups, vendor patches, and KrebsOnSecurity / The Record.

sources.name: USGS, Copernicus EMS & NOAA Environmental Telemetry
sources.ownership_and_funding: European Union Copernicus Programme, U.S. Geological Survey (https://www.usgs.gov), and U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (https://www.noaa.gov).
sources.editorial_standards: Calibrated physical sensor networks: seismographs, Sentinel-1/2 SAR and optical satellite imagery, ocean buoys, and atmospheric CO2/methane observatories.
strengths: Objective physical telemetry for earthquakes, floods, wildfires, gas flaring, ship wakes, flood extent, and global temperature anomalies
known_limitations_and_biases: Automated preliminary sensor alerts (e.g., initial earthquake magnitudes or thermal hotspot detections) undergo human geophysical review; SAR/optical interpretation requires domain care (cloud cover, resolution limits)
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Distinguish automated preliminary sensor detections from reviewed geophysical products, and pair single-event weather telemetry with peer-reviewed attribution science.

sources.name: OFAC SDN, EU Sanctions Map & UN Consolidated Sanctions
sources.ownership_and_funding: European External Action Service, U.S. Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control (https://ofac.treasury.gov), and UN Security Council Sanctions Committees.
sources.editorial_standards: Legally binding entity, vessel (IMO number), aircraft tail, and crypto-wallet designations with statutory citations and general licenses.
strengths: Definitive verification of whether an entity, bank, semiconductor tool, or shadow-fleet oil tanker is legally sanctioned, and under which jurisdiction (multilateral UN vs. unilateral US/EU)
known_limitations_and_biases: Treasury designation press releases state executive-branch evidentiary allegations that are rarely tested in full adversarial criminal trials
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Treat legal designation status as confirmed fact (A1), while treating underlying intelligence allegations in press releases as official state attribution requiring independent OSINT corroboration.

sources.name: Open Aviation & Maritime Telemetry (ADS-B / AIS Registries)
sources.ownership_and_funding: Crowdsourced VHF/transponder receiver networks (ADS-B Exchange, OpenSky Network https://opensky-network.org, MarineTraffic / IMO GISIS).
sources.editorial_standards: Raw unedited radio transponder broadcasts (ICAO hex codes, MMSI/IMO vessel identifiers, altitude/speed/heading tracks).
strengths: Real-time verification of military/diplomatic flights, chokepoint maritime traffic (Red Sea, Hormuz, Panama, Taiwan Strait), and vessel diversion patterns
known_limitations_and_biases: Susceptible to GPS/GNSS spoofing, AIS 'going dark' (transponder shutoff), MMSI identity laundering, and terrestrial receiver coverage gaps over open oceans
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Never treat AIS/ADS-B absence as proof a vessel/aircraft left an area, and verify anomalous coordinates against GNSS-spoofing zones and synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery.
